questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A shopkeeper buys an article for ₹500 and sells it for ₹600. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Profit = SP - CP = 600 - 500 = ₹100. Profit% = (Profit/CP) × 100 = (100/500) × 100 = 20%. Option 16.67% calculates profit on SP instead of CP. Option 25% uses wrong base. Option 10% divides by 1000 instead of 500.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about profit and loss:

(i) Profit percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price.
(ii) If SP > CP, there is a profit.
(iii) If SP < CP, there is a loss.
(iv) Discount is always calculated on the Selling Price.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Profit% is calculated on CP (i correct). SP > CP means profit (ii correct). SP < CP means loss (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — discount is calculated on the MARKED PRICE (MRP), not the Selling Price. SP = MP - Discount.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If an article is sold at a loss of 10%, the selling price is 90% of the cost price.
Reason (R): Loss percentage means the fraction of cost price that is lost, so SP = CP × (100 - Loss%)/100.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — 10% loss means SP = CP - 10% of CP = 90% of CP. Reason (R) is correct — the formula SP = CP × (100 - Loss%)/100 gives 90% when loss = 10%. The formula in (R) directly derives the result in (A). Option B is wrong because (R) is the formula that explains (A). Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Match the following terms with their definitions:

Column I:
(a) Cost Price
(b) Selling Price
(c) Marked Price
(d) Discount

Column II:
(i) The price at which an article is sold to the customer
(ii) The reduction given on the marked price
(iii) The price at which an article is purchased
(iv) The price displayed on the label of an article

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Cost Price is the purchase price (a-iii). Selling Price is what the customer pays (b-i). Marked Price is the label/tag price (c-iv). Discount is the reduction from marked price (d-ii). Option B swaps CP with SP. Option C swaps SP with MP. Option D incorrectly pairs CP with label price.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Which of the following result in a profit of exactly 25%?

(i) CP = ₹400, SP = ₹500
(ii) CP = ₹800, SP = ₹1000
(iii) CP = ₹600, SP = ₹750
(iv) CP = ₹1200, SP = ₹1400

Select the correct combination:

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: An article marked at ₹800 is sold at a discount of 15%. What is the selling price?
questions.explanation: Discount = 15% of 800 = ₹120. SP = MP - Discount = 800 - 120 = ₹680. Option ₹720 uses 10% discount. Option ₹660 uses 17.5% discount. Option ₹700 uses 12.5% discount.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) If a trader buys at ₹200 and sells at ₹180, his loss is ₹20.
(ii) Loss percentage in the above case is 10%.
(iii) To make 20% profit on CP of ₹200, the SP should be ₹240.
(iv) If SP equals CP, neither profit nor loss occurs.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Loss = 200-180 = ₹20 (i correct). Loss% = 20/200 × 100 = 10% (ii correct). 20% profit on ₹200: SP = 200 + 40 = ₹240 (iii correct). When SP = CP, profit = 0 and loss = 0 (iv correct). All statements are mathematically accurate.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A man buys a bicycle for ₹3,000 and sells it at a loss of 20%. What is the selling price?
questions.explanation: Loss = 20% of 3000 = ₹600. SP = CP - Loss = 3000 - 600 = ₹2,400. Option ₹2,500 uses 16.67% loss. Option ₹2,600 uses 13.3% loss. Option ₹2,200 uses 26.67% loss.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above the cost price and gives a discount of 20%. His net profit is 12%.
Reason (R): Net SP = CP × (1 + 40/100) × (1 - 20/100) = CP × 1.4 × 0.8 = 1.12 × CP, giving 12% profit.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — marking up 40% then discounting 20% gives: MP = 1.4×CP, SP = 0.8×1.4×CP = 1.12×CP → 12% profit. Reason (R) correctly shows the mathematical derivation. The calculation in (R) proves (A). Option B is wrong because (R) mathematically proves (A). Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: If the selling price of 12 articles equals the cost price of 15 articles, what is the profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Let CP of 1 article = ₹1. CP of 15 = ₹15. SP of 12 = ₹15 (given). SP of 1 = 15/12 = ₹1.25. Profit = 1.25 - 1 = ₹0.25. Profit% = 0.25/1 × 100 = 25%. Option 20% uses wrong ratio. Option 30% miscalculates. Option 15% uses (15-12)/15 incorrectly.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A trader buys goods worth ₹5,000 and spends ₹500 on transportation. If he sells the goods for ₹6,600, his profit percentage is:
questions.explanation: Total CP = Purchase + Transport = 5000 + 500 = ₹5,500. Profit = 6600 - 5500 = ₹1,100. Profit% = (1100/5500) × 100 = 20%. Option 32% uses only purchase price as base. Option 10% miscalculates. Option 15% uses wrong profit figure.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about successive discounts:

(i) Two successive discounts of 10% and 20% are equivalent to a single discount of 28%.
(ii) Successive discounts of 20% and 10% give the same result as 10% and 20%.
(iii) Two successive discounts of 10% each are equivalent to a single discount of 20%.
(iv) The order of successive discounts does not affect the final price.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Two discounts 10% and 20%: effective = 100 - (100×0.9×0.8) = 100-72 = 28% (i correct). Order doesn't matter in multiplication: 0.9×0.8 = 0.8×0.9 (ii and iv correct). Statement (iii) is incorrect — two 10% discounts: 0.9×0.9 = 0.81, so effective discount = 19%, NOT 20%.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A fruit seller buys oranges at ₹5 each and sells them at ₹7 each. How many oranges must he sell to make a profit of ₹200?
questions.explanation: Profit per orange = 7 - 5 = ₹2. Number of oranges for ₹200 profit = 200/2 = 100. Option 80 gives profit of ₹160. Option 50 gives profit of ₹100. Option 120 gives profit of ₹240.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Match the following scenarios with their profit/loss percentages:

Column I:
(a) CP = ₹250, SP = ₹300
(b) CP = ₹400, SP = ₹360
(c) CP = ₹500, SP = ₹625
(d) CP = ₹800, SP = ₹720

Column II:
(i) 10% loss
(ii) 25% profit
(iii) 20% profit
(iv) 10% loss

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a): (300-250)/250×100 = 20% profit (a-iii). (b): (400-360)/400×100 = 10% loss (b-i). (c): (625-500)/500×100 = 25% profit (c-ii). (d): (800-720)/800×100 = 10% loss (d-iv). Option B mismatches (a) with 25%. Option C swaps (b) and (d). Option D incorrectly starts with loss for (a).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A dealer offers a discount of 10% on the marked price and still makes a profit of 8%. If the marked price is ₹600, what is the cost price?
questions.explanation: SP = MP - 10% discount = 600 - 60 = ₹540. If profit is 8%, then SP = 1.08 × CP → 540 = 1.08 × CP → CP = 540/1.08 = ₹500. Option ₹540 is the SP, not CP. Option ₹480 uses 12% profit. Option ₹520 uses wrong calculation.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: If an article is purchased for ₹1,500 and sold for ₹1,800, the profit is ₹__________ and profit percentage is __________.
questions.explanation: Profit = 1800 - 1500 = ₹300. Profit% = (300/1500) × 100 = 20%. Option '300, 16.67%' calculates on SP instead of CP. Option '200, 20%' gets wrong profit amount. Option '300, 25%' uses wrong denominator (1200).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A television is sold for ₹18,000 at a loss of 10%. What was the cost price?
questions.explanation: SP = CP × (100-Loss%)/100 → 18000 = CP × 90/100 → CP = 18000 × 100/90 = ₹20,000. Option ₹19,800 adds 10% to SP (wrong method). Option ₹18,900 adds ₹900. Option ₹21,000 uses wrong percentage.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) When two articles are sold at the same price, one at 20% profit and the other at 20% loss, there is an overall loss.
(ii) The overall loss percentage in such a case is 4%.
(iii) When both profit and loss percentages are equal and SP is the same, there is always a net loss.
(iv) The net loss percentage = (common%)²/100.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: When SP is same with equal profit% and loss%: CP₁ = SP/1.2, CP₂ = SP/0.8. Total CP > Total SP always (i, iii correct). Loss% = (20)²/100 = 4% (ii, iv correct). All statements accurately describe this classic profit-loss scenario. The formula (common%)²/100 gives the net loss percentage.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A shopkeeper sells an article at 10% profit. Had he sold it for ₹36 more, he would have gained 25%. The cost price is:

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A man sells two articles for ₹990 each; on one he gains 10% and on the other he loses 10%. He has an overall loss.
Reason (R): When SP is the same and gain% = loss%, net loss always occurs because the cost price of the loss-making article is higher than that of the profit-making one.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — CP₁ = 990/1.1 = 900, CP₂ = 990/0.9 = 1100. Total CP = 2000, Total SP = 1980, Net loss = ₹20. Reason (R) is correct — the article sold at loss had higher CP (1100 > 900), making total CP exceed total SP. The asymmetry explained in (R) is why the loss occurs (A). Option B is wrong because (R) explains the mechanism. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A merchant marks his goods at 50% above cost price and allows a discount of 20%. His profit percentage is:
questions.explanation: MP = 1.5 × CP. SP = MP × 0.8 = 1.5 × 0.8 × CP = 1.2 × CP. Profit% = 20%. Option 30% forgets the discount. Option 25% miscalculates. Option 15% uses wrong markup-discount combination.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the cost price and selling price of 5 items sold by a trader:

A → 200, 250
B → 300, 270
C → 150, 180
D → 400, 500
E → 250, 225

On how many items did the trader make a profit?
questions.explanation: Item A: SP(250) > CP(200) → Profit ✓. Item B: SP(270) < CP(300) → Loss ✗. Item C: SP(180) > CP(150) → Profit ✓. Item D: SP(500) > CP(400) → Profit ✓. Item E: SP(225) < CP(250) → Loss ✗. Profit on 3 items (A, C, D). Option 2 miscounts. Option 4 includes one loss item. Option 5 is impossible.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: If the cost price of 25 articles is equal to the selling price of 20 articles, then the profit percentage is:
questions.explanation: Let CP of 1 article = ₹1. CP of 25 articles = ₹25. SP of 20 articles = ₹25. SP of 1 article = 25/20 = ₹1.25. Profit = 0.25. Profit% = (0.25/1) × 100 = 25%. Option 20% uses (25-20)/25. Option 30% miscalculates. Option 5% uses (25-20)/100.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about marked price and discount:

(i) SP = MP × (100 - Discount%)/100.
(ii) If no discount is given, SP = MP.
(iii) A shopkeeper can make profit even after giving a discount if MP > CP.
(iv) Discount percentage is always calculated on the cost price.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: SP = MP × (100-D%)/100 is the correct formula (i correct). No discount means SP = MP (ii correct). If MP is sufficiently above CP, profit exists even after discount (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — discount is calculated on MARKED PRICE, not cost price.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A man bought a horse for ₹10,000. At what price should he sell it to gain 15%?
questions.explanation: SP = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100 = 10000 × 115/100 = ₹11,500. Option ₹11,000 gives only 10% profit. Option ₹12,000 gives 20% profit. Option ₹10,500 gives only 5% profit.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Successive discounts of 10% and 20% on a marked price of ₹1000 result in a final selling price of ₹720.
Reason (R): After the first discount of 10%, the price becomes ₹900, and then 20% off ₹900 gives ₹720.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — 1000 × 0.9 × 0.8 = 720. Reason (R) is correct — it shows the step-by-step: 1000→900 (after 10%), then 900→720 (after 20%). The stepwise calculation in (R) proves (A). Option B is wrong because (R) demonstrates the calculation for (A). Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A shopkeeper bought 80 kg of rice at ₹40/kg and sold it at ₹50/kg. His total profit is:
questions.explanation: Total CP = 80 × 40 = ₹3200. Total SP = 80 × 50 = ₹4000. Profit = 4000 - 3200 = ₹800. Option ₹1000 uses profit of ₹12.5/kg. Option ₹600 uses wrong quantity. Option ₹400 uses profit of ₹5/kg.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Match the following situations with their profit/loss outcomes:

Column I:
(a) MP = ₹500, Discount = 10%, CP = ₹400
(b) CP = ₹300, SP = ₹270
(c) MP = ₹1000, Discount = 25%, CP = ₹800
(d) CP = ₹600, Profit% = 15%

Column II:
(i) SP = ₹690
(ii) 12.5% profit
(iii) 10% loss
(iv) SP = ₹750, Loss of ₹50

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a): SP = 500×0.9 = 450, Profit = (450-400)/400×100 = 12.5% (a-ii). (b): Loss = (300-270)/300×100 = 10% (b-iii). (c): SP = 1000×0.75 = 750, Loss = 800-750 = ₹50 (c-iv). (d): SP = 600×1.15 = ₹690 (d-i). Option B swaps (a) and (b). Option C mismatches (c) with loss percentage. Option D incorrectly places (a) with ₹750.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A man sells an article at a profit of 30%. If he had bought it for 10% less and sold it for ₹198 less, he would have made a profit of 20%. The original cost price is:

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: If a shopkeeper sells goods at cost price using a weight of 900 grams instead of 1 kg, his profit percentage is:
questions.explanation: He charges for 1000g but gives only 900g. Profit on 900g transaction = 100g worth. Profit% = (100/900) × 100 = 11.11%. Option 10% uses 100/1000. Option 9% miscalculates. Option 12.5% uses wrong ratio. The profit is calculated on his actual cost (900g), not on what he charges (1000g).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A dealer sells a TV for ₹15,000, making a profit of 25%. What is the cost price?
questions.explanation: SP = CP × (100+25)/100 → 15000 = CP × 1.25 → CP = 15000/1.25 = ₹12,000. Option ₹11,250 = 15000/1.33. Option ₹13,000 subtracts only 2000. Option ₹10,000 uses 50% profit calculation.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about break-even:

(i) Break-even occurs when total revenue equals total cost.
(ii) At break-even, profit is zero.
(iii) Break-even means the selling price equals the cost price per unit.
(iv) Beyond break-even, every additional sale adds to loss.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: At break-even, revenue = cost (i correct), so profit = 0 (ii correct), meaning SP = CP per unit in simple terms (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — beyond break-even, additional sales add to PROFIT (not loss), because fixed costs are already covered.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A book is listed at ₹450 and a discount of 20% is given. A sales tax of 10% is charged on the discounted price. The customer pays:
questions.explanation: Discounted price = 450 × 0.8 = ₹360. Sales tax = 10% of 360 = ₹36. Customer pays = 360 + 36 = ₹396. Option ₹405 calculates tax on MP. Option ₹360 forgets tax. Option ₹414 uses wrong discount.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
The following data shows monthly sales of a shop:

Jan → 100, 50, 60
Feb → 80, 50, 55
Mar → 120, 50, 65

In which month was the total profit the highest?
questions.explanation: Jan profit: 100 × (60-50) = 100 × 10 = ₹1,000. Feb profit: 80 × (55-50) = 80 × 5 = ₹400. Mar profit: 120 × (65-50) = 120 × 15 = ₹1,800. March has the highest total profit at ₹1,800. January is ₹1,000. February is ₹400.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A trader mixes 20 kg of rice bought at ₹30/kg with 30 kg of rice bought at ₹40/kg. At what price per kg should he sell the mixture to gain 10%?
questions.explanation: Total CP = (20×30) + (30×40) = 600 + 1200 = ₹1800. Total quantity = 50 kg. CP per kg = 1800/50 = ₹36. For 10% profit: SP per kg = 36 × 1.1 = ₹39.60. Option ₹38.50 uses wrong profit%. Option ₹37.40 uses ~4% profit. Option ₹40 uses 11.11% profit.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A single discount of 30% is NOT equivalent to two successive discounts of 15% each.
Reason (R): Two successive discounts of 15% give an effective discount of 27.75% (not 30%), since the second discount applies to the already-reduced price.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — 30% single ≠ two 15% successive discounts. Reason (R) is correct — effective = 100 - (0.85×0.85×100) = 100 - 72.25 = 27.75%, which is less than 30%. The mathematical explanation in (R) proves WHY they're not equivalent (A). Option B is wrong because (R) directly proves (A). Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A shopkeeper bought 5 dozen pens at ₹20 each and sold them at ₹25 each. His total profit is:
questions.explanation: 5 dozen = 60 pens. Total CP = 60 × 20 = ₹1200. Total SP = 60 × 25 = ₹1500. Profit = 1500 - 1200 = ₹300. Option ₹250 uses 50 pens. Option ₹350 uses wrong SP. Option ₹200 uses 40 pens.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: If an article is sold at a 25% profit on its cost price of ₹800, the selling price is ₹__________.
questions.explanation: SP = CP + 25% of CP = 800 + 200 = ₹1000. Or SP = 800 × 1.25 = ₹1000. Option ₹1050 adds 31.25%. Option ₹900 adds only 12.5%. Option ₹1100 adds 37.5%.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Which of the following statements are true about a sale where MP = ₹1000, Discount = 20%, and CP = ₹700?

(i) The selling price is ₹800.
(ii) The profit is ₹100.
(iii) The profit percentage is approximately 14.3%.
(iv) The trader incurs a loss.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: SP = 1000 × 0.8 = ₹800 (i correct). Profit = 800 - 700 = ₹100 (ii correct). Profit% = 100/700 × 100 = 14.28% ≈ 14.3% (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — there is a PROFIT of ₹100, not a loss.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A merchant had 100 kg of sugar. He sold a part at 7% profit and the rest at 17% profit, making an overall profit of 10%. How much was sold at 7% profit?
questions.explanation: Let x kg sold at 7%. Then (100-x) kg at 17%. Overall: 7x + 17(100-x) = 10×100 → 7x + 1700 - 17x = 1000 → -10x = -700 → x = 70 kg. Option 60: 7×60+17×40=420+680=1100 (11% average, not 10%). Option 50: gives 12% average. Option 80: gives 9% average.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: The cost price of an article is ₹500. It is marked up by 40% and then a discount of 15% is given. The net profit is:
questions.explanation: MP = 500 × 1.4 = ₹700. After 15% discount: SP = 700 × 0.85 = ₹595. Profit = 595 - 500 = ₹95. Option ₹100 would need SP of ₹600 (discount of 14.3%). Option ₹97 would need SP of ₹597. Option ₹90 would need SP of ₹590 (discount of 15.7%).

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A trader sells goods at 20% above cost price but uses a weight of 800 grams instead of 1000 grams. His actual profit percentage is:
questions.explanation: He charges 120% of CP for what should be 1 kg but gives only 800g. Effective: He pays for 800g at CP rate = 0.8×CP. He receives 1.2×CP (selling at 20% profit on full kg rate). Profit on actual cost = (1.2CP - 0.8CP)/0.8CP × 100 = 0.4/0.8 × 100 = 50%. Option 40% doesn't account for both factors. Option 45% averages the two. Option 35% uses wrong calculation.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) If an article costing ₹400 is sold for ₹480, the profit% is 20%.
(ii) If an article costing ₹500 is sold for ₹450, the loss% is 10%.
(iii) If profit is 50% and SP is ₹750, then CP is ₹500.
(iv) If loss is 25% and CP is ₹800, then SP is ₹600.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
The following data shows sales of a shopkeeper over 3 days:

Mon → 20, 80, 95
Tue → 15, 90, 100
Wed → 10, 100, 120

What is the total profit earned over the 3 days?
questions.explanation: Mon profit: 20 × (95-80) = 20 × 15 = ₹300. Tue profit: 15 × (100-90) = 15 × 10 = ₹150. Wed profit: 10 × (120-100) = 10 × 20 = ₹200. Total profit = 300 + 150 + 200 = ₹650. Option ₹600 miscalculates Wed profit. Option ₹700 overcounts. Option ₹550 undercounts.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A person buys a watch for ₹2,000 and sells it for ₹1,600. The loss percentage is:

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Match the following:

Column I:
(a) SP = ₹450, Profit = 12.5%
(b) SP = ₹720, Loss = 10%
(c) CP = ₹350, Profit = 20%
(d) CP = ₹900, Loss = 15%

Column II:
(i) CP = ₹800
(ii) SP = ₹420
(iii) CP = ₹400
(iv) SP = ₹765

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a): CP = 450/1.125 = 400 (a-iii). (b): CP = 720/0.9 = 800 (b-i). (c): SP = 350×1.2 = 420 (c-ii). (d): SP = 900×0.85 = 765 (d-iv). Option B swaps all incorrectly. Option C mismatches (b) and (d). Option D shuffles all pairs wrongly.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A shopkeeper allows a 10% discount on the marked price of goods and still makes a profit of 20%. If his cost price is ₹600, what is the marked price?
questions.explanation: For 20% profit: SP = 600 × 1.2 = ₹720. SP = MP × 0.9 (after 10% discount) → 720 = MP × 0.9 → MP = 720/0.9 = ₹800. Option ₹720 is the SP, not MP. Option ₹750 uses wrong discount rate. Option ₹900 uses 20% discount calculation.

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements:

(i) If an article is bought for ₹1000 and overhead expenses are ₹200, the total CP is ₹1200.
(ii) Overhead expenses (transport, repairs, etc.) are added to the purchase price to get the true cost price.
(iii) Profit/loss should be calculated on the total cost price including overheads.
(iv) Overhead expenses are always exactly 10% of the purchase price.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Total CP = purchase + overheads = 1000+200 = ₹1200 (i correct). Overhead expenses like transport/repairs are added to get true CP (ii correct). Profit/loss is calculated on total CP (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — overhead expenses vary case by case; they are NOT always exactly 10% of purchase price.

questions.subject: D

questions.subject: D
questions.questionText: A man purchased two articles for ₹3,000 each. He sold one at a profit of 10% and the other at a loss of 10%. What is the overall result?
questions.explanation: Article 1: SP = 3000 × 1.1 = ₹3300 (profit ₹300). Article 2: SP = 3000 × 0.9 = ₹2700 (loss ₹300). Total SP = 3300 + 2700 = ₹6000. Total CP = 3000 + 3000 = ₹6000. Net result = 0 (no profit, no loss). NOTE: When COST PRICE is the same (not SP) and gain% = loss%, the result is always zero. Option B/C are wrong — those apply when SP is same with equal profit/loss.
